extractions.extraction_text: insidious onset of muscle spasms in the left calf and stiffness in his calf muscles; symptoms increased progressively over three years involving muscles of the arms and legs; spasms and stiffness exacerbated by sudden, rapid body movements and emotional upset; hypertrophy and spasm of the paraspinal muscles; hyperlordosis; marked reduction in spinal mobility; boardlike rigidity of the abdomen; hyperreflexia and fasciculations; limping, guarded gait; sensory examination was normal

workup performed for various neuromuscular disorders including myotonic dystrophy, fibromyositis, benign cramp and fasciculation syndrome, lipid or glycogen storage disease, McArdle's disease, and chronic lead poisoning; diagnosed as having a personality disorder with somatization
spasms, rigidity and stiffness of the axial and limb musculature, occasionally worsened spasms and stiffness
Electromyography revealed persistent motor unit activity at rest, particularly of the lower limbs, with inability of paraspinal and limb musculature to relax; stiff-man syndrome was finally diagnosed
treatment with 50 mg/day of oral diazepam, gradually increased to 60 mg/day
marked improvement with a decrease in muscle spasms and stiffness; spasms and stiffness relieved by additional doses of diazepam; patient remains alert, with no sedation
Electromyography of the involved muscles (usually paraspinal and limb muscles) characteristically reveals persistent involuntary motor unit discharges at rest within ability to relax
history of psychological problems
